rendered: The premise is reversed. The document says the 10% Mn[1] sample delivered the higher capacity, not the 50% Mn[2] sample: 212 mAh g^− 1 (10% Mn)[3] versus 164 mAh g^− 1[4]. The heat results follow the same pattern: the 10% Mn[5] sample released 901.4 J g^−1[6] in thermal decomposition, against 485.7 J g^−1[7]. So the 10% Mn[8] sample released more heat, by 415.7[9] J/g, about 1.86[10] times the heat output of the 50% Mn[11] sample. These heat values are for delithiated electrodes, per the text on that page.
